**Scott Edward Parazynski** (born July 28, 1961) is an American physician and former NASAastronaut. A veteran of five Space Shuttle flights and seven spacewalks, Parazynski's latest mission was STS-120 in October 2007 – highlighted by a dramatic, unplanned extra-vehicular activity (EVA) to repair a live solar array. In May 2016, he was inducted into the United States Astronaut Hall of Fame. He retired from NASA in March 2009 to pursue entrepreneurial opportunities in the private sector, and he is currently the CEO of a technology start-up. He is the first person to have both flown in space and summited Mount Everest, the highest point on Earth.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scott_E._Parazynski#cite_note-1) He describes his life's experiences in his 2017 memoir _The Sky Below_.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scott_E._Parazynski#cite_note-2)
texts.1: Parazynski is of Polish descent, as his great-great-grandparents migrated from Kraków to the US.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scott_E._Parazynski#cite_note-se-3) He considers Palo Alto, California, and Evergreen, Colorado, to be his hometowns. He is married to Meenakshi Wadhwa, a planetary scientist at Arizona State University. He has two children with his first wife, Gail. Scott enjoys mountaineering, rock climbing, flying and scuba diving. A commercial, multi-engine, seaplane and instrument-rated pilot, Parazynski has logged over 2500 flight hours in a variety of aircraft. As a mountaineer, his summits include Cerro Aconcagua (at 22,841 feet (6,962 m) above sea level, the tallest mountain in the world outside Asia) and all 59 of Colorado's peaks over 14,000 feet (4,300 m) in altitude. He first attempted to summit Mount Everest in May 2008, but was forced to turn back before the summit due to a severe back injury. Serving as team physician for the Discovery Channel[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scott_E._Parazynski#cite_note-4) a year later, at 4:00 am on May 20, 2009, he successfully summited the 29,029 feet (8,848 m) mountain.
texts.2: Other notable expeditions include a scientific dive into the summit caldera lake atop Licancabur Volcano (19,409 feet (5,916 m) on the Bolivian-Chilean border), one of the world's highest lakes, and setting the first bootprints adjacent Masaya Volcano's lava lake in Nicaragua with Sam Cossman in 2016.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scott_E._Parazynski#cite_note-5) He also travelled aboard OceanGate's submersible _Titan_ and visited the wreck of the _Titanic_ in the North Atlantic.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scott_E._Parazynski#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scott_E._Parazynski#cite_note-7)

## Education and early life
[edit]
Parazynski attended junior high school at Dakar Academy in Dakar, Senegal, and Beirut, Lebanon. In March 1969 as an eight-year-old, he travelled to Florida to witness the launch of Apollo 9, an event he argued inspired him to pursue a career in science. He attended high school at the Community School, Tehran, Iran, and the American Community School, Athens, Greece, graduating in 1979. He received a Bachelor of Science degree in biology from Stanford University in 1983, continuing on to graduate with honors from Stanford Medical School in 1989. He served his medical internship at the [Brigham and Women's Hospital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brigham_and_Women's_Hospital "Brigham and Women's Hospital") of Harvard Medical School (1990). He had completed 22 months of a residency program in emergency medicine in Denver, Colorado, when selected for the NASA Astronaut Corps.
Parazynski is a Fellow of the Aerospace Medical Association and The Explorers Club. Additionally, he is a member of the American Society for Gravitational and Space Biology, the Wilderness Medical Society, the American Alpine Club, the Association of Space Explorers, the Experimental Aircraft Association, and the Aircraft Owners and Pilots Association. He is president of the board of directors of the Challenger Center for Space Science Education, and serves on the boards of the Houston Museum of Natural Science, the University of Texas McDonald Observatory and OceanGate.
In 2014, Parazynski was appointed as a professor of practice at Arizona State University, and was designated ASU's first University Explorer.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scott_E._Parazynski#cite_note-8) He subsequently founded Fluidity Technologies[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scott_E._Parazynski#cite_note-9) based on his intellectual property, a company aiming to manufacture and distribute novel control devices for mobility in 3D space, for everything from drones and computer games to virtual reality and surgical robotics.

HAPPY 62nd BIRTHDAY TO ASTRONAUT SCOTT PARAZYNSKI
With whopping five Space Shuttle missions and 58 days in space in his life, we wish spacewalker Scott Parazynski a happy 62nd birthday. He is the first person to have both flown in space (7 spacewalks!), and climbed to the summit of Mount Everest, the highest point on Earth.
Scott was born in Little Rock, Arkansas on July 28, 1961, but he grew up in Palo Alto, California and Evergreen, Colorado .Among Parazynski’s seven spacewalks totaling 47 hours, is a dramatic, unplanned EVA to repair a live solar array on STS-120, his last flight in 2007.
A competitor in the luge (sled) trails of the 1988, he became an Olympic Team Coach for the Philippines during the 1988 Olympic Winter Games in Calgary, Canada, and later, as Honorary Captain of the United States Olympic Luge Team during the 2010 Olympic Winter Games in Vancouver, Canada.

## [PDF page 1]
While in medical school, Dr.  Parazynski  competed on the United States Development Luge Team and was ranked among the top  
10 competitors in the nation during the 1988 Olympic Trials.  He also served as an Olympic Team Coach for the Philippines  
during the 1988 Olympic Winter Games in Calgary, Canada,  and later, as Honorary Captain of the United States Olympic Luge  
T eam during the 2010 Olympic Winter Games in Vancouver, Canada.
EXPERIENCE:  While an undergraduate at Stanford University, Dr. Parazynski studied antigenic variation in African Sleeping  
Sickness, using sophisticated molecular biological techniques. While in medical school, he was awarded a NASA Graduate  
Student Fellowship and conducted research at NASA-Ames Research Center on fluid shifts that occur during human spaceflight.  
Additionally, he has been involved in the design of several exercise devices that are being developed for long-duration  
spaceflight, and  he  has conducted research on high-altitude acclimatization.  Dr. Parazynski has numerous publications in the  
field of space physiology and has a particular expertise in human adaptation to stressful environments.  He has also invented a  
number of medical devices and other technologies for life in extreme environments.
NASA EXPERIENCE:  Selected as an astronaut in March 1992, Dr. Parazynski reported to the Johnson Space Center in August  
1992.  He completed one year of training and evaluation and was qualified as a mission specialist.  Dr. Parazynski initially served

Cosmonaut T raining Center, Star City, Russia.  In October 1995, when sitting-height parameters raised concerns  about his fitting  
safely in the Soyuz vehicle in the event of an emergency aboard the Mir station, he was deemed too tall for the mission and was  
withdrawn from Mir training.  He has served as the Astronaut Office crew representative for space  shuttle,  space  station and  
Soyuz training, as Deputy (Operations and Training) of the Astronaut Office ISS Branch, and as Chief of the Astronaut Office  
EVA Branch.  In the aftermath of the Columbia tragedy, he was the Astronaut Office l  ead for s  pace  shuttle  thermal  protection  
sys t e m  inspection and r  epair.  A veteran of five spaceflights, STS-66 (1994), STS-86 (1997), STS-95 (1998), STS-100 (2001)

during  seven  spacewalks, and has  traveled  more than  23 million miles.  Dr. Parazynski retired from NASA in March 2009 to  
work in private industry and to pursue other entrepreneurial and exploration interests.

**Scott Edward Parazynski** (born July 28, 1961) is an American physician and former NASAastronaut. A veteran of five Space Shuttle flights and seven spacewalks, Parazynski's latest mission was STS-120 in October 2007 – highlighted by a dramatic, unplanned extra-vehicular activity (EVA) to repair a live solar array. In May 2016, he was inducted into the United States Astronaut Hall of Fame. He retired from NASA in March 2009 to pursue entrepreneurial opportunities in the private sector, and he is currently the CEO of a technology start-up. He is the first person to have both flown in space and summited Mount Everest, the highest point on Earth.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scott_E._Parazynski#cite_note-1) He describes his life's experiences in his 2017 memoir _The Sky Below_.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scott_E._Parazynski#cite_note-2)

Parazynski is of Polish descent, as his great-great-grandparents migrated from Kraków to the US.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scott_E._Parazynski#cite_note-se-3) He considers Palo Alto, California, and Evergreen, Colorado, to be his hometowns. He is married to Meenakshi Wadhwa, a planetary scientist at Arizona State University. He has two children with his first wife, Gail. Scott enjoys mountaineering, rock climbing, flying and scuba diving. A commercial, multi-engine, seaplane and instrument-rated pilot, Parazynski has logged over 2500 flight hours in a variety of aircraft. As a mountaineer, his summits include Cerro Aconcagua (at 22,841 feet (6,962 m) above sea level, the tallest mountain in the world outside Asia) and all 59 of Colorado's peaks over 14,000 feet (4,300 m) in altitude. He first attempted to summit Mount Everest in May 2008, but was forced to turn back before the summit due to a severe back injury. Serving as team physician for the Discovery Channel[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scott_E._Parazynski#cite_note-4) a year later, at 4:00 am on May 20, 2009, he successfully summited the 29,029 feet (8,848 m) mountain.

Other notable expeditions include a scientific dive into the summit caldera lake atop Licancabur Volcano (19,409 feet (5,916 m) on the Bolivian-Chilean border), one of the world's highest lakes, and setting the first bootprints adjacent Masaya Volcano's lava lake in Nicaragua with Sam Cossman in 2016.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scott_E._Parazynski#cite_note-5) He also travelled aboard OceanGate's submersible _Titan_ and visited the wreck of the _Titanic_ in the North Atlantic.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scott_E._Parazynski#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scott_E._Parazynski#cite_note-7)

## Education and early life
[edit]
Parazynski attended junior high school at Dakar Academy in Dakar, Senegal, and Beirut, Lebanon. In March 1969 as an eight-year-old, he travelled to Florida to witness the launch of Apollo 9, an event he argued inspired him to pursue a career in science. He attended high school at the Community School, Tehran, Iran, and the American Community School, Athens, Greece, graduating in 1979. He received a Bachelor of Science degree in biology from Stanford University in 1983, continuing on to graduate with honors from Stanford Medical School in 1989. He served his medical internship at the [Brigham and Women's Hospital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brigham_and_Women's_Hospital "Brigham and Women's Hospital") of Harvard Medical School (1990). He had completed 22 months of a residency program in emergency medicine in Denver, Colorado, when selected for the NASA Astronaut Corps.
Parazynski is a Fellow of the Aerospace Medical Association and The Explorers Club. Additionally, he is a member of the American Society for Gravitational and Space Biology, the Wilderness Medical Society, the American Alpine Club, the Association of Space Explorers, the Experimental Aircraft Association, and the Aircraft Owners and Pilots Association. He is president of the board of directors of the Challenger Center for Space Science Education, and serves on the boards of the Houston Museum of Natural Science, the University of Texas McDonald Observatory and OceanGate.
In 2014, Parazynski was appointed as a professor of practice at Arizona State University, and was designated ASU's first University Explorer.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scott_E._Parazynski#cite_note-8) He subsequently founded Fluidity Technologies[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scott_E._Parazynski#cite_note-9) based on his intellectual property, a company aiming to manufacture and distribute novel control devices for mobility in 3D space, for everything from drones and computer games to virtual reality and surgical robotics.

Jamahl Mosley is the Head Coach of the New Orleans Pelicans. On May 18, 2026, Mosley became the 9th Head Coach* in Pelicans history.
Prior to joining the Pelicans, Coach Mosley was the Head Coach of the Orlando Magic (2021-2026), where he led the team to three consecutive NBA Playoff berths (2024, 2025, 2026). Prior to joining the Magic, he was an Assistant Coach for the Dallas Mavericks under Head Coach Rick Carlisle (2014-2021), where he helped the team reach four NBA Playoff berths (2015, 2016, 2020, 2021). Prior to joining the Mavericks, Coach Mosley was an Assistant Coach for the Cleveland Cavaliers under Head Coaches Byron Scott (2010-2013) and Mike Brown (2013-2014). Prior to joining the Mavericks, he was a Player Development/Advance Scout (2005-2007) and an Assistant Coach (2007-2010) with the Denver Nuggets under Head Coach George Karl, where he helped the team reach at least 50 wins for three consecutive seasons (2007-2010), and five NBA Playoff berths (2006 2007, 2008, 2009, 2010), including an NBA Conference Finals appearance (2009).
Jamahl Mosley was born on October 6, 1978, in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. He attended and played at the University of Colorado, where he was selected to the Third-Team All-Big 12 (2000 & 2001). Coach Mosley also had a professional playing career with stops overseas in Australia, Spain, and Korea.

### NEW ORLEANS PELICANS HEAD COACH
Jamahl Mosley is the Head Coach of the New Orleans Pelicans. On May 18, 2026, Mosley became the 9th Head Coach* in Pelicans history.
Prior to joining the Pelicans, Coach Mosley was the Head Coach of the Orlando Magic (2021-2026), where he led the team to three consecutive NBA Playoff berths (2024, 2025, 2026). Prior to joining the Magic, he was an Assistant Coach for the Dallas Mavericks under Head Coach Rick Carlisle (2014-2021), where he helped the team reach four NBA Playoff berths (2015, 2016, 2020, 2021). Prior to joining the Mavericks, Coach Mosley was an Assistant Coach for the Cleveland Cavaliers under Head Coaches Byron Scott (2010-2013) and Mike Brown (2013-2014). Prior to joining the Mavericks, he was a Player Development/Advance Scout (2005-2007) and an Assistant Coach (2007-2010) with the Denver Nuggets under Head Coach George Karl, where he helped the team reach at least 50 wins for three consecutive seasons (2007-2010), and five NBA Playoff berths (2006 2007, 2008, 2009, 2010), including an NBA Conference Finals appearance (2009).
Jamahl Mosley was born on October 6, 1978, in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. He attended and played at the University of Colorado, where he was selected to the Third-Team All-Big 12 (2000 & 2001). Coach Mosley also had a professional playing career with stops overseas in Australia, Spain, and Korea.

_**As of Mar. 15, 2024**_
**Jamahl****Mosley**, the head coach of the Orlando Magic, fufilled his first head coaching assignment with USA Basketball as the head coach of the 2023 Men's Select Team. The team, made up of NBA and NBA G League talent, trainined with and against the 2023 Men's National Team ahead of the 2023 FIBA World Cup. This was his second time serving on a select team coaching staff. He was an assisntant with the 2021 Men's Select Team prior to the 2020 Olympic Games.
Mosley was named the head coach of the Magic in 2021. He was an assistant coach with the Dallas Mavericks prior to Orlando and also served as the head coach of Dallas' Summer League squad from 2017-19.
Mosley spent four seasons as an assistant coach for the Cleveland Cavaliers from 2010-14. Before joining the Cavaliers in July 2010, Mosley spent five seasons with the Denver Nuggets. His tenure began in player development and advance scouting before he became an assistant coach for his last three seasons with the franchise. The Nuggets reached the playoffs, winning 50 games or more, each of his final three years.
A native of Milwaukee, Mosley was a four-year letterman at University of Colorado (1997-2001). Named in 2000 All-Big 12 Conference third team, he is one of 33 players in CU history to score more than 1,000 points. Following his collegiate career, he played four seasons of professional basketball overseas, including two years for the Victoria Titans (Australia), one year with Baloncesto Leon (Spain) and one year in South Korea.

**Jamahl Malcolm Mosley** (born October 6, 1978) is an American professional basketball coach and former player who is the head coach of the New Orleans Pelicans of the National Basketball Association (NBA). He played college basketball for the [Colorado Buffaloes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Buffaloes_men's_basketball "Colorado Buffaloes men's basketball") and professionally for four seasons overseas.
Mosley began his coaching career in 2005 as a player development coach for the Denver Nuggets. He was promoted to assistant coach in 2007 and served in the same capacity for the Cleveland Cavaliers and Dallas Mavericks. After seven years with the Mavericks, Mosley was hired as head coach for the Orlando Magic in 2021.
Mosley was born on October 6, 1978, in Milwaukee as the second child to parents James and Deborah Mosley.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamahl_Mosley#cite_note-OrlandoSentinel_Price2022-1) His parents divorced when he was 6 and he moved to San Diego with his mother and brother when he was 13.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamahl_Mosley#cite_note-OrlandoSentinel_Price2022-1) Mosley attended Rancho Buena Vista High School, where he was named the California Interscholastic Federation Player of the Year in 1997.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamahl_Mosley#cite_note-OrlandoSentinel_Price2022-1)

Mosley played college basketball for the [Colorado Buffaloes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Buffaloes_men's_basketball "Colorado Buffaloes men's basketball") and was a third-team All-Big 12 selection in 2000.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamahl_Mosley#cite_note-Big12Conference_RecordBook-2) He began his career in Mexico with Petroleros de Salamanca in 2001 before he joined the Victoria Titans of the Australian National Basketball League (NBL) and was named the league's Best Sixth Man in 2002.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamahl_Mosley#cite_note-ddl-3) Mosley signed with Baloncesto León in 2003 and played there for one season.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamahl_Mosley#cite_note-ddl-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamahl_Mosley#cite_note-pb-4) He split the 2004–05 season with Korihait in Finland and the Seoul Samsung Thunders in South Korea where he finished his playing career.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamahl_Mosley#cite_note-pb-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamahl_Mosley#cite_note-5)

Mosley joined the Denver Nuggets of the NBA as a player development coach and scout in 2005.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamahl_Mosley#cite_note-dm-6) He was promoted to an assistant coach in 2007.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamahl_Mosley#cite_note-dm-6) Mosley worked as an assistant coach for the Cleveland Cavaliers from 2010 to 2014.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamahl_Mosley#cite_note-dm-6) He joined the Dallas Mavericks as an assistant coach in 2014.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamahl_Mosley#cite_note-dm-6) Mosley became the Mavericks' defensive coordinator in 2018.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamahl_Mosley#cite_note-dm-6) On April 2, 2021, he served as acting head coach after Rick Carlisle had a positive COVID-19 test and led the Mavericks to a 99–86 victory over the New York Knicks.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamahl_Mosley#cite_note-TheDallasMorningNews_Townsend2021-7)

### Orlando Magic (2021–2026)
[edit]
On July 11, 2021, Mosley was named as head coach of the Orlando Magic.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamahl_Mosley#cite_note-8) In his introductory press conference, Mosley said he wanted a pass-oriented offense that "play[s] with pace", and a "disruptive" defense with strong communication between the players.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamahl_Mosley#cite_note-9)
On March 12, 2024, Mosley agreed to a four-year extension with the Magic.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamahl_Mosley#cite_note-10) After the Magic blew a 3–1 series lead against the Detroit Pistons in the first round of the 2026 NBA playoffs, Mosley was fired on May 4, 2026.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamahl_Mosley#cite_note-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamahl_Mosley#cite_note-12)

### New Orleans Pelicans (2026–present)
[edit]
On May 18, 2026, after being fired by the Magic, the New Orleans Pelicans hired Mosley as head coach to replace interim head coach James Borrego.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamahl_Mosley#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamahl_Mosley#cite_note-14)

### NEW ORLEANS PELICANS HEAD COACH
Jamahl Mosley is the Head Coach of the New Orleans Pelicans. On May 18, 2026, Mosley became the 9th Head Coach* in Pelicans history.
Prior to joining the Pelicans, Coach Mosley was the Head Coach of the Orlando Magic (2021-2026), where he led the team to three consecutive NBA Playoff berths (2024, 2025, 2026). Prior to joining the Magic, he was an Assistant Coach for the Dallas Mavericks under Head Coach Rick Carlisle (2014-2021), where he helped the team reach four NBA Playoff berths (2015, 2016, 2020, 2021). Prior to joining the Mavericks, Coach Mosley was an Assistant Coach for the Cleveland Cavaliers under Head Coaches Byron Scott (2010-2013) and Mike Brown (2013-2014). Prior to joining the Mavericks, he was a Player Development/Advance Scout (2005-2007) and an Assistant Coach (2007-2010) with the Denver Nuggets under Head Coach George Karl, where he helped the team reach at least 50 wins for three consecutive seasons (2007-2010), and five NBA Playoff berths (2006 2007, 2008, 2009, 2010), including an NBA Conference Finals appearance (2009).
Jamahl Mosley was born on October 6, 1978, in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. He attended and played at the University of Colorado, where he was selected to the Third-Team All-Big 12 (2000 & 2001). Coach Mosley also had a professional playing career with stops overseas in Australia, Spain, and Korea.

### NEW ORLEANS PELICANS HEAD COACH
Jamahl Mosley is the Head Coach of the New Orleans Pelicans. On May 18, 2026, Mosley became the 9th Head Coach* in Pelicans history.
Prior to joining the Pelicans, Coach Mosley was the Head Coach of the Orlando Magic (2021-2026), where he led the team to three consecutive NBA Playoff berths (2024, 2025, 2026). Prior to joining the Magic, he was an Assistant Coach for the Dallas Mavericks under Head Coach Rick Carlisle (2014-2021), where he helped the team reach four NBA Playoff berths (2015, 2016, 2020, 2021). Prior to joining the Mavericks, Coach Mosley was an Assistant Coach for the Cleveland Cavaliers under Head Coaches Byron Scott (2010-2013) and Mike Brown (2013-2014). Prior to joining the Mavericks, he was a Player Development/Advance Scout (2005-2007) and an Assistant Coach (2007-2010) with the Denver Nuggets under Head Coach George Karl, where he helped the team reach at least 50 wins for three consecutive seasons (2007-2010), and five NBA Playoff berths (2006 2007, 2008, 2009, 2010), including an NBA Conference Finals appearance (2009).
Jamahl Mosley was born on October 6, 1978, in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. He attended and played at the University of Colorado, where he was selected to the Third-Team All-Big 12 (2000 & 2001). Coach Mosley also had a professional playing career with stops overseas in Australia, Spain, and Korea.
***Inclusive of Full-Time and Interim Head Coaches**

**Jamahl Malcolm Mosley** (born October 6, 1978) is an American professional basketball coach and former player who is the head coach of the New Orleans Pelicans of the National Basketball Association (NBA). He played college basketball for the [Colorado Buffaloes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Buffaloes_men's_basketball "Colorado Buffaloes men's basketball") and professionally for four seasons overseas.
Mosley began his coaching career in 2005 as a player development coach for the Denver Nuggets. He was promoted to assistant coach in 2007 and served in the same capacity for the Cleveland Cavaliers and Dallas Mavericks. After seven years with the Mavericks, Mosley was hired as head coach for the Orlando Magic in 2021.
Mosley was born on October 6, 1978, in Milwaukee as the second child to parents James and Deborah Mosley.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamahl_Mosley#cite_note-OrlandoSentinel_Price2022-1) His parents divorced when he was 6 and he moved to San Diego with his mother and brother when he was 13.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamahl_Mosley#cite_note-OrlandoSentinel_Price2022-1) Mosley attended Rancho Buena Vista High School, where he was named the California Interscholastic Federation Player of the Year in 1997.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamahl_Mosley#cite_note-OrlandoSentinel_Price2022-1)

Mosley played college basketball for the [Colorado Buffaloes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Buffaloes_men's_basketball "Colorado Buffaloes men's basketball") and was a third-team All-Big 12 selection in 2000.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamahl_Mosley#cite_note-Big12Conference_RecordBook-2) He began his career in Mexico with Petroleros de Salamanca in 2001 before he joined the Victoria Titans of the Australian National Basketball League (NBL) and was named the league's Best Sixth Man in 2002.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamahl_Mosley#cite_note-ddl-3) Mosley signed with Baloncesto León in 2003 and played there for one season.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamahl_Mosley#cite_note-ddl-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamahl_Mosley#cite_note-pb-4) He split the 2004–05 season with Korihait in Finland and the Seoul Samsung Thunders in South Korea where he finished his playing career.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamahl_Mosley#cite_note-pb-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamahl_Mosley#cite_note-5)

Mosley joined the Denver Nuggets of the NBA as a player development coach and scout in 2005.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamahl_Mosley#cite_note-dm-6) He was promoted to an assistant coach in 2007.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamahl_Mosley#cite_note-dm-6) Mosley worked as an assistant coach for the Cleveland Cavaliers from 2010 to 2014.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamahl_Mosley#cite_note-dm-6) He joined the Dallas Mavericks as an assistant coach in 2014.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamahl_Mosley#cite_note-dm-6) Mosley became the Mavericks' defensive coordinator in 2018.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamahl_Mosley#cite_note-dm-6) On April 2, 2021, he served as acting head coach after Rick Carlisle had a positive COVID-19 test and led the Mavericks to a 99–86 victory over the New York Knicks.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamahl_Mosley#cite_note-TheDallasMorningNews_Townsend2021-7)

### Orlando Magic (2021–2026)
[edit]
On July 11, 2021, Mosley was named as head coach of the Orlando Magic.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamahl_Mosley#cite_note-8) In his introductory press conference, Mosley said he wanted a pass-oriented offense that "play[s] with pace", and a "disruptive" defense with strong communication between the players.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamahl_Mosley#cite_note-9)
On March 12, 2024, Mosley agreed to a four-year extension with the Magic.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamahl_Mosley#cite_note-10) After the Magic blew a 3–1 series lead against the Detroit Pistons in the first round of the 2026 NBA playoffs, Mosley was fired on May 4, 2026.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamahl_Mosley#cite_note-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamahl_Mosley#cite_note-12)

### New Orleans Pelicans (2026–present)
[edit]
On May 18, 2026, after being fired by the Magic, the New Orleans Pelicans hired Mosley as head coach to replace interim head coach James Borrego.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamahl_Mosley#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamahl_Mosley#cite_note-14)

### NEW ORLEANS PELICANS HEAD COACH
Jamahl Mosley is the Head Coach of the New Orleans Pelicans. On May 18, 2026, Mosley became the 9th Head Coach* in Pelicans history.
Prior to joining the Pelicans, Coach Mosley was the Head Coach of the Orlando Magic (2021-2026), where he led the team to three consecutive NBA Playoff berths (2024, 2025, 2026). Prior to joining the Magic, he was an Assistant Coach for the Dallas Mavericks under Head Coach Rick Carlisle (2014-2021), where he helped the team reach four NBA Playoff berths (2015, 2016, 2020, 2021). Prior to joining the Mavericks, Coach Mosley was an Assistant Coach for the Cleveland Cavaliers under Head Coaches Byron Scott (2010-2013) and Mike Brown (2013-2014). Prior to joining the Mavericks, he was a Player Development/Advance Scout (2005-2007) and an Assistant Coach (2007-2010) with the Denver Nuggets under Head Coach George Karl, where he helped the team reach at least 50 wins for three consecutive seasons (2007-2010), and five NBA Playoff berths (2006 2007, 2008, 2009, 2010), including an NBA Conference Finals appearance (2009).
Jamahl Mosley was born on October 6, 1978, in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. He attended and played at the University of Colorado, where he was selected to the Third-Team All-Big 12 (2000 & 2001). Coach Mosley also had a professional playing career with stops overseas in Australia, Spain, and Korea.
